plates.side_label: 1957–1997 TIMELINE · HADLOW/GAJDUSEK/ALPERS KURU, ALPER/GRIFFITH UV PROOF, PRUSINER PRIONS, WEISSMANN KNOCKOUT MICE & TEMPLATE BLOCKING
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 5 Sep 1959 & 19 Feb 1966 (William Hadlow links sheep scrapie to kuru; Carleton Gajdusek & Michael Alpers prove kuru is a slow transmissible spongiform encephalopathy, winning the 1976 Nobel Prize) · 20 May & 9 Sep 1967 (Tikvah Alper proves the scrapie agent survives nucleic-acid-shredding UV and ionizing radiation; John Stanley Griffith proposes self-replicating protein folding) · 9 Apr 1982, 19 Apr 1985 & 2 Jul 1993 (Stanley Prusiner isolates PrP and coins 'prion'; Prusiner, Hood & Weissmann find the PRNP gene in normal DNA; Charles Weissmann's Prnp0/0 knockout mice prove the protein-domino hypothesis and win Prusiner the 1997 Nobel Prize).

teach_overlay.label: 1957–1997 PRIONS TIMELINE · PROTEIN-TEMPLATED REFOLDING IN NEUROLOGY & BENEFICIAL YEAST PRION MEMORY
teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1957 → 1997) alongside a diagram showing therapeutic antibodies capping the PrPC-to-PrPSc contact interface to halt template propagation
teach_overlay.scale: from mountain villages in Papua New Guinea to a radiation chamber in London and knockout mice in Zurich, prions proved that biological information can hide not just in a string of DNA letters, but in the 3D fold of a single protein
